title: The economic impact of the UK's beer and pub industry
author: Sanele Mjikane
text:

The economic impact of the UK’s beer and pub industry

The beer and pub industry plays an important role within the UK economy both culturally and economically.

We completed an economic impact assessment of the beer and pub industry across the UK, capturing the separate impact of the breweries, pubs, off-trade and the rest of the on-trade sectors. The approach isolated the industry’s total impacts across the UK at both local authority and parliamentary constituency levels. We also completed Scottish and Welsh reports as part of this, with the latter translated into Welsh.

The beer and pub industry plays an important role within the UK economy both culturally and economically. Pubs are at the heart of many local communities, spread across the length and breadth of the country. Yet the total footprint of the industry is greater than just pubs, as it also considers the brewing of beer, as well as the sales of beer throughout hotels, restaurants, sports clubs, and in the retail trade. The beer and pub industry, therefore, has a footprint in every local community across the country.

To understand the current scale of its economic footprint in the UK economy, the British Beer and Pub Association (BBPA) commissioned Oxford Economics to update our economic impact analysis of the industry. These estimates consider the impacts from four subsectors of beer and pub activity. These are the brewing of beer, the activity of pubs, the proportion of activity in the rest of the on-trade (excluding pubs) that is attributable to the sale of beer, and the share of the off-trade that is dependent on beer sales.

Key findings from the report:

We estimate the beer and pub industry generated a total of £37.8 billion in gross value added (GVA) contributions to UK GDP in 2025.

The beer and pub industry supported almost 1 million jobs across the UK in 2025, and £21.2 billion in employee compensation.

In 2025, Oxford Economics estimate that the UK’s beer and pub sector directly employed 711,300 people, supporting £11.7 billion in employee compensation, and generating £18.6 billion in GVA contributions to GDP.

The beer and pub sector provides a vital source of employment for the young and those seeking to work part-time. Across the UK, 341,900 workers between the ages of 16 and 24 year were employed in the beer and pub industry in 2025. This represents almost half (48%) of total direct employment in the sector, compared to just 11% across the UK economy more broadly.
